name: Background Page Processing (Execution Chain)
apex: A page process type that runs a chain of child processes asynchronously via the database job scheduler, so users do not wait for long operations like data loads.
workflow: Create an Execution Chain process, add child processes under it, enable Execute in Background, then monitor via Developer Toolbar > Session > Background Executions.
relevance: Backend async job orchestration tied to Oracle's DB scheduler; Paddock Developer's scope is page composition, looks and themes, not server job execution.
skip_for_web: DBMS_SCHEDULER-specific; no page-design or theming angle.

name: Shared Component Subscriptions
apex: A master/subscriber relationship letting many apps in a workspace reuse one shared component (LOVs, lists, auth schemes, etc) by subscribing to a master copy and refreshing or publishing changes.
workflow: Copy a component from another app with Copy and Subscribe, then later click Refresh (per-component) or Publish (master pushes to all) to sync changes.
relevance: Useful if Paddock ever keeps a master copy of a component (e.g. a page template) reused elsewhere with explicit refresh/publish control instead of always-live references.

name: Static ID Dependency Resolution
apex: When copying, subscribing, refreshing or publishing, APEX matches a dependent shared component to an existing one first by Static ID, then by name; if no match, it copies the dependency in.
workflow: Give a shared component a stable Static ID so APEX can re-identify the same component across apps or environments during copy or refresh, instead of duplicating it.
relevance: A stable Static ID per component, not just its name, is the right key for Paddock Developer to track the same component across preview/prod environments or versions.

name: Lists of Values (LOV)
apex: A named, reusable list of display/return value pairs, static or dynamic, that any page item or report column can reference to render as radio group, select list, checkboxes, etc.
workflow: Shared Components > Lists of Values > Create; define static rows or a dynamic query, then reference it from a page item's List of Values attribute.
relevance: Directly maps to a reusable options-list component Paddock Developer needs for admin form fields (e.g. session type, tyre compound) shared across many forms.

name: Creating a Static List of Values
apex: Wizard step that defines a named static LOV as an ordered set of manually entered display/return value pairs, then binds it to a page item as e.g. a Radio Group.
attributes: Create List of Values: From Scratch
Item List of Values Type: Shared Component
workflow: Create List of Values Wizard > From Scratch > Static > enter display/return rows in sequence > save; then set an item's List of Values to that shared list.
relevance: Same static-options pattern Paddock Developer needs for hardcoded choice sets (e.g. flag status); confirms return value defaults to display value if left blank.

name: Creating a Dynamic List of Values
apex: Wizard step that defines a named LOV whose options are queried live from a table, SQL query, PL/SQL function, or REST source rather than hardcoded.
attributes: Data Source: Local Database/REST Enabled SQL/REST Data Source
Source Type: Table/SQL Query/PL-SQL Function Returning SQL
workflow: Create List of Values Wizard > Dynamic > pick a data source and source type > map return/display columns > save; bind to an item as e.g. a Select List.
relevance: Matches Paddock's need for options that come from live content (e.g. pick a driver from the drivers table) instead of a hardcoded list.

name: Editing / Bulk-Editing a List of Values
apex: Edit a single LOV's definition on its edit page, or bulk-edit every static LOV's display text at once from a Grid Edit tab.
workflow: Shared Components > Lists of Values > click a list to edit fully, or open Grid Edit to mass-edit display text across all static LOVs.
relevance: The Grid Edit bulk-editing idea, a spreadsheet-like edit of many small values at once, is a useful admin UX pattern for Paddock's own options/label management.

name: Copying or Subscribing to a List of Values
apex: Wizard that copies a List of Values from another application in the workspace, with an option to copy-and-subscribe so the copy stays linked to its master for future refresh.
workflow: Lists of Values page > Tasks > Copy from another app > pick source app > choose Copy or Copy and Subscribe > Copy List of Values.
relevance: Solves cross-application duplication inside one workspace; Paddock is a single app with one shared LOV store, so there is nothing to copy between.
skip_for_web: cross-app copy workflow, not applicable to a single-app site

name: Subscribing to a List of Values (standalone page)
apex: Same subscribe/refresh/unsubscribe steps as the Subscription region covered under Editing an Existing List of Values; duplicate content, no new settings.
relevance: Duplicate of the Subscription region steps already logged; no new setting or concept beyond Static ID resolution.
skip_for_web: duplicate page

name: Referencing Session State Within a List of Values
apex: Best practice of using a bind variable (e.g. :P1_DEPTNO) in a dynamic LOV's query so the list filters by another item's current value.
attributes: Bind variable syntax (:ITEM_NAME) inside LOV SQL
workflow: Write the LOV query with a bind variable referencing another page item so the list narrows based on that item's current value.
relevance: Cascading option lists, e.g. pick a session after picking an event, need the same dependency-on-another-field pattern in Paddock Developer's dynamic lists.

name: Lists of Values Reports
apex: Tabbed reports on the Lists of Values page for auditing and maintaining LOVs across an application.
workflow: Shared Components > Lists of Values > switch tabs to find locally-defined LOVs worth promoting to shared, bulk-edit null text, or see utilization and history.
relevance: The Utilization tab (where is this used) and History tab (recent changes) are exactly the auditing views Paddock Developer's own shared Lists/Component Settings should offer.

name: Deleting a List
apex: Removes a shared List component from Shared Components; deleting it also deletes any List regions built from it.
workflow: Shared Components > Lists > select a list to open List Details, then click Delete.
relevance: The cascading-delete warning, deleting a shared List also deletes regions built on it, is exactly the guardrail Paddock Developer needs before an operator deletes a shared List.

name: Copying or Subscribing to a List
apex: Wizard that duplicates a shared List within the same app or from another application, optionally subscribing to keep the copy linked to its source.
workflow: Lists page > Tasks > Copy from another app (or the Copy column) > choose source app and list > name the copy > optionally enable Subscribe > Copy.
relevance: Duplicate-within-app-under-a-new-name is a useful Paddock Developer action to start a new List from an existing one; the cross-app subscribe half does not apply to a single-app site.
skip_for_web: cross-application subscribe half not applicable to a single-app site

name: Subscribing to a List (List Details page)
apex: Same subscribe/refresh/unsubscribe mechanism as other shared components, applied to Lists via the List Details page Subscription region.
relevance: Same subscription mechanism already logged for Lists of Values and the general Shared Component Subscriptions model; no new concept.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: List Reports
apex: Tabbed reports on the Lists page (Unused, Conditional Entries, Subscription, Utilization, History) plus a Grid Edit view of all entries for one list.
workflow: Shared Components > Lists > pick a report tab to audit usage, or open a list's Grid Edit to mass-edit its entries.
relevance: The Unused tab, flagging Lists nothing references, is a valuable cleanup view Paddock Developer should offer for its own shared Lists and components.

name: Example Search Pages
apex: Illustrates that a search page's Search field can sit in different template positions, a Breadcrumb region or After Logo between logo and nav bar, with a Search Results region in the page Body, or be assembled manually.
workflow: Built via the Create Page Wizard's Search Page type, or assembled manually by placing a search item and a results region with Search Sources.
relevance: Confirms a sitewide search box is just a positioned input plus a results region driven by named sources, a good shape for a Paddock Developer global-search component.

name: Oracle Text Index (search prerequisite)
apex: A database full-text index (CREATE INDEX ... INDEXTYPE IS CTXSYS.CONTEXT) built via SQL Commands before an Oracle TEXT search configuration can use it.
workflow: Run a CREATE INDEX statement in SQL Workshop > SQL Commands on the column to be searched.
relevance: Oracle Text is a database-engine feature; Paddock's content lives outside Oracle so this specific indexing technology cannot be reused.
skip_for_web: Oracle Text/CTXSYS is Oracle-DB-specific full-text indexing

name: Search Configuration
apex: A named, reusable definition of one searchable data source (table, SQL, or REST) with column mappings, stored in Shared Components and referenced by one or more Search Sources on search pages.
attributes: Search Type: Standard/Oracle TEXT/Oracle Ubiquitous Search/List
workflow: Shared Components > Search Configurations > Create; pick a search type and source, map title/description/key columns, then set the result Link Type and Page.
relevance: This is the exact shape Paddock Developer's global search needs: one reusable searchable-source definition (title/description/link) per content type, independent of the results UI.

name: Creating a Search Page (Create Page Wizard)
apex: Wizard that builds a page with a Search field and a Search Results region wired to one or more chosen Search Configurations.
workflow: Create Page > Search Page > name it, pick Search Configurations, create; Page Designer shows the search item plus a Search Results region containing one Search Source per configuration.
relevance: A single search page federating multiple Search Sources, e.g. drivers, races, posts, into one Results region is the right pattern for a Paddock sitewide search page.

name: Ubiquitous Search Index (DBMS_SEARCH)
apex: A JSON-based full-text index built across multiple tables and columns in one index using the DBMS_SEARCH PL/SQL package (requires Oracle AI Database 26ai), letting one Search Configuration cover several sources at once.
workflow: Run DBMS_SEARCH.CREATE_INDEX then ADD_SOURCE per table in SQL Commands, then build a Search Configuration of type Oracle Ubiquitous Search against that index.
relevance: A database engine feature requiring Oracle AI Database 26ai; Paddock has no equivalent DB and would implement cross-content search at the application layer instead.
skip_for_web: Oracle-DB-specific (DBMS_SEARCH, 26ai requirement)

name: Oracle Vector Search
apex: Semantic search over a table's VECTOR column: an embedding model (Vector Provider) converts text to vectors stored per row, then a Search Configuration matches a query's embedding against them by similarity instead of exact text.
workflow: Add a VECTOR column, backfill embeddings via a Vector Provider, then create a Search Configuration of type Oracle Vector Search mapping the vector, title and description columns.
relevance: The pattern, embed content once and match by similarity, is directly reusable for a future Paddock semantic search over articles or drivers using Supabase pgvector, even though the Oracle VECTOR type and API are not.
skip_for_web: VECTOR column type and APEX_AI package are Oracle-specific; Paddock would need pgvector or similar.

name: Editing a Search Configuration (attributes)
apex: The Search Configuration Edit page's full attribute set: label, query prefix, source query, text-query parsing mode, column mapping, icon, link, and access-control conditions.
attributes: Text Query Function: None/Progressive Relaxation/Expert Search/Custom
workflow: Shared Components > Search Configurations > select one > edit Settings, Source, Column Mapping, Icon/Link and Advanced groups > Apply Changes.
relevance: Search Query Prefix (scope a search to one source by typing a keyword) and the None/Progressive-Relaxation/Expert text-query modes are strong ideas for Paddock's own federated search UX.

name: Copying or Subscribing to a Search Configuration
apex: Wizard to duplicate a Search Configuration within the same app or copy one from another application, optionally subscribing to track its master; copying without subscribing generates a fresh Static ID.
workflow: Search Configurations page > Copy column (same app) or Tasks > Copy from another app > name the new label > optionally Subscribe > Copy.
relevance: Duplicating a Search Configuration as a starting point for a new content-type search is a useful same-app action for Paddock Developer; the cross-app subscribe half does not apply.
skip_for_web: cross-application subscribe half not applicable to a single-app site

name: Subscribing to a Search Configuration (standalone page)
apex: Same subscribe/refresh/unsubscribe steps as other shared components, applied to Search Configurations via their Edit page Subscription region.
relevance: Same subscription mechanism already logged for Lists, Lists of Values and the general model; no new concept.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: Search Results Region and Search Sources
apex: A search page's Search Results region (Region Type = Search) contains one child Search Source per Search Configuration added to the page; each source maps to one configuration and can be styled or behave independently.
workflow: Page Designer > select the Search Results region for region-wide settings, or select a nested Search Source to configure just that one content type.
relevance: Confirms the right nesting for Paddock Developer's own search results: one results region, many named sources such as drivers, races, posts, each independently configurable.

name: Search Results Attributes
apex: Settings on the Search Results region controlling how the whole federated search behaves: which item holds the query, live-typing, pagination, sort order, empty and no-results messages, and lazy loading.
attributes: Results per Page Type: Static Value/Based on Item Value
workflow: Page Designer > Search Results region > Attributes tab > set Settings, Pagination, Appearance, Sort, Messages and Performance groups.
relevance: Search-as-you-type with a minimum-character threshold, lazy loading, and explicit empty and no-results messages are exactly the polish Paddock Developer's search component needs.

name: Search Source Attributes
apex: Per-source settings on a Search Source nested in the Search Results region, such as which icon or badge decorates that source's results.
workflow: Page Designer > select a Search Source under the Search Results region > set its Icon and Badge in the Property Editor.
relevance: Per-content-type result icons, e.g. a car icon for drivers versus a flag for races, is a small but real detail Paddock Developer's search result cards should support.

name: Search Configuration Reports
apex: Utilization and History tabs on the Search Configurations page showing where each configuration is used and its recent edit history.
workflow: Shared Components > Search Configurations > click Utilization or History tab.
relevance: Same Utilization and History auditing pattern Paddock Developer should apply consistently across all its shared component types, including search.

name: Component Groups
apex: A named bundle of existing shared components (Lists, LOVs, REST Data Sources, Auth Schemes, etc) that can be copied, subscribed, refreshed, published or deleted together as one unit instead of one at a time.
workflow: Shared Components > Component Groups > Create, name it, then Assign Components picking a Component Type and moving items into the group.
relevance: A Component Group is the right unit for Paddock Developer to export/import or duplicate a whole feature's worth of shared components, e.g. a List plus its Component Settings, together.

name: Component Group Copy/Refresh/Publish Action Resolution
apex: When copying, refreshing or publishing a component group, APEX previews a per-component Action, Add, Refresh, Refresh and Assign, Replace, Reuse, or Unassign, so the developer sees exactly what will change before confirming.
workflow: Start a group copy, refresh or publish; review the generated Action per component in the preview table, then confirm to apply.
relevance: A preview-before-apply diff of what will be added, changed or removed is exactly the safety net Paddock Developer needs for any bulk component operation.

name: Deleting a Component Group
apex: Deletes the group and its component assignments only; the individual shared components that were members remain untouched in the application.
workflow: Component Groups page > select group > Edit page > Delete > confirm.
relevance: The contrast with deleting a List, which cascade-deletes its regions, matters: Paddock Developer should make clear whether deleting a grouping ever deletes members or only ungroups them.

name: Static Application Files Location (#APP_FILES# Path)
apex: An advanced User Interface Attribute that redirects the #APP_FILES# substitution string to a web server or CDN URL instead of the database, for performance.
workflow: Shared Components > User Interface Attributes > Advanced tab > set #APP_FILES# Path to a CDN or web-server URL, or leave blank to serve from the database.
relevance: Paddock already serves static assets from Cloudflare/Next.js public folders and R2, not a database-backed file store, so this DB-vs-CDN switch has no equivalent decision to make.
skip_for_web: solves a database-hosted-files problem Paddock does not have

name: Referencing Static Application Files (#APP_FILES#)
apex: A substitution string that resolves to the current application's static file base path wherever used in HTML, CSS or URLs.
workflow: Type #APP_FILES#/filename.ext in any template, region source or URL target to link to an app-scoped static file.
relevance: Paddock uses normal asset imports and URLs (Next.js public folder, R2 URLs) rather than a template substitution-string system for file paths.
skip_for_web: substitution-string mechanism specific to APEX template rendering

name: Static Application Files (Database-Stored File Manager)
apex: A per-application file manager in Shared Components for uploading, browsing, downloading and deleting small static assets, images, CSS, JS, stored inside the database.
workflow: Shared Components > Static Application Files > Create File, set directory and drag a file in; browse, download or delete from the report view; Download as Zip for everything.
relevance: The shape of an in-app asset manager, directory field, drag-drop upload, size and mime report, zip-all download, bulk delete, is a strong template for a Paddock Developer media library.

name: Static Application Files in Remote Storage (OCI Object Storage)
apex: Lets an app's static files live in an OCI Object Storage bucket instead of the database, wired up via a Remote File Storage definition and OCI credentials, with optional migration and ongoing sync.
attributes: Synchronize Files: From Object Storage to Local Database/From Local Database to Object Storage
workflow: Edit Application Definition > Add Object Storage > fill in bucket and credential details > optionally migrate existing files > later use Synchronize Files to keep both sides current.
relevance: Paddock already stores media in R2; the two-way Synchronize Files direction toggle and a Static-ID-identified storage definition are good ideas for a Paddock Developer asset-storage settings screen.
skip_for_web: OCI-specific bucket, compartment and credential mechanics do not transfer

name: Static Workspace Files
apex: Same file manager as Static Application Files, upload, report, download, delete, but scoped to the whole workspace and referenced via #WORKSPACE_FILES#, so any application in that workspace can use them.
workflow: Shared Components > Static Workspace Files > Create File; any app in the workspace can then reference the file via #WORKSPACE_FILES#.
relevance: The app-vs-workspace file-scope split solves multi-app asset sharing; Paddock is a single app or site so its one media library already covers this without a second tier.
skip_for_web: duplicate file-manager UI already logged at the application level; workspace scoping does not apply to a single app

name: Report Query
apex: A named, reusable Shared Component that pairs a SQL data source with an output format (PDF, Word, Excel, HTML, XML) and an optional Report Layout, so any button or link can trigger a formatted document download.
attributes: Report Query Source: Local Database/REST Enabled SQL/REST Source/Duality View/JSON Source
workflow: Shared Components > Report Queries > Create; pick a layout, output format and data source, then point a button, list item or branch at the generated URL to trigger the download.
relevance: The reusable export-definition idea, one Shared Component wiring a query to a downloadable PDF or Excel format, is a clean pattern for a future Paddock export-standings or download-results feature.
skip_for_web: the specific print-server integrations (Document Generator, BI Publisher, AOP) are Oracle infrastructure Paddock does not run

name: Report Layouts
apex: A reusable print-formatting template, a Shared Component, attached to a report region or Report Query to render data as a formatted document instead of the default layout.
attributes: Report Layout Type: Generic Columns (XSL-FO)/Named Columns (XSL-FO)
workflow: Shared Components > Report Layouts > Create; choose Generic Columns to auto-fit any query, or upload a Named Columns XSL-FO/RTF file for pixel-precise custom layouts, then attach the layout to a report or report query.
relevance: The Generic-vs-Named-Columns split, an auto-fit default versus an uploaded custom template, mirrors the choice Paddock Developer's export/print feature should offer between a quick default and a fully custom layout.
skip_for_web: XSL-FO/RTF markup and specific print-server format lists (BI Publisher, AOP) are Oracle print-engine details

name: Copying or Subscribing to a Report Layout
apex: Same copy-within-app and copy-and-subscribe-from-another-app mechanism already covered for Lists, LOVs and Search Configurations, applied here to Report Layouts.
relevance: Same copy/subscribe mechanism already logged multiple times for other shared component types; no new concept.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: Subscribing to Email Templates
apex: Same subscribe/refresh/unsubscribe mechanism as other shared components, applied to Email Templates via their Details page Subscription region.
relevance: Same subscription mechanism already logged for multiple component types; no new concept, and this page does not cover authoring an email template itself.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: Sample Data (built-in datasets)
apex: Ready-made read-only datasets (Employees, Geolocation, Time-Based) usable as a Data Source when building any page component, so a developer can build and preview a page before real data exists.
attributes: SQL Workshop > Utilities > Sample Datasets (installable/editable copies)
workflow: In Create Page Wizard or Page Designer, set a component's Data Source to Sample Data to prototype with realistic rows, or install an editable copy via SQL Workshop for a working sample app.
relevance: A built-in placeholder or sample dataset for prototyping a new region before real content exists is a genuinely useful onboarding feature for Paddock Developer to offer new component types.

name: Data Load Definition
apex: A reusable Shared Component describing how to import CSV, XLSX, XML or JSON into a table or collection: a data profile that maps file columns to target columns with optional lookups or transformation rules.
attributes: Sample Data (Upload a File/Copy and Paste)
Data Profile Columns: SQL Expression/SQL Query/Lookups/Transformation Rules
When on Error: Ignore/Stop/Log Error into Collection/Log into Error Log
workflow: Shared Components > Data Load Definitions > Create; upload a sample file to auto-map columns, set the loading method and error handling, then optionally auto-create a Data Loading page.
relevance: A reusable upload-and-map definition, auto column mapping, Append/Merge/Replace, error handling, is exactly what Paddock Developer needs for admin-side bulk import of a season's calendar, drivers or results.
skip_for_web: DML error logging table mechanics are Oracle-specific; Paddock would log failed rows to its own store instead.

name: Data Loading Page
apex: A single generated page, built from a Data Load Definition, that lets a user upload or paste a file, preview the parsed rows, and click Load Data to run the import.
attributes: Upload Data From: File/Copy and Paste
workflow: Create Page > Data Loading > pick an existing Data Load Definition and a max file size; the generated page handles upload, preview and load.
relevance: The upload-preview-confirm workflow, drag a file, see parsed rows before committing, is the right UX shape for a Paddock Developer bulk-import screen.

name: Copying or Subscribing to a Data Load Definition
apex: Same cross-application copy and subscribe wizard already covered for other shared component types, applied to Data Load Definitions.
relevance: Same copy and subscribe mechanism already logged multiple times; no new concept.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: Collections
apex: A session-scoped temporary bucket for storing and naming arbitrary rows of data mid-workflow, e.g. across a multi-step wizard, before committing them to the database, manipulated via the APEX_COLLECTION API.
workflow: Insert rows into a named collection as a user progresses through a wizard or bulk-edit page, then run a final process that applies the collection's contents to real tables.
relevance: The concept, hold draft multi-row edits in temporary session state until a final Save, is worth copying for any Paddock Developer multi-step form, e.g. building a season's full session list before committing.
skip_for_web: APEX_COLLECTION itself is an Oracle PL/SQL package; Paddock would hold this in its own session or DB draft table.

name: Working with Duality Views and JSON Sources (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents page pointing to Managing Duality Views and Managing JSON Sources subtopics; no settings of its own.
relevance: Pure navigation page; the real content is in the linked Duality Views subtopic.
skip_for_web: navigational index only, no distinct settings

name: Duality Views
apex: A local or remote database object combining relational and JSON-document access to the same data; APEX wraps one as a Duality View Source with an auto-derived Data Profile so page components can consume it like any other data source.
attributes: Location: Local Database/REST Enabled SQL Service
workflow: Shared Components > Duality Views > Create; pick the database's duality view object, confirm the auto-derived Data Profile's primary key columns, then use it as a data source anywhere in the app.
relevance: JSON-relational Duality Views are an Oracle AI Database 26ai engine feature with no equivalent in Paddock's Supabase/Postgres stack.
skip_for_web: requires Oracle AI Database 26ai; database-engine-specific object type

name: REST Data Sources (overview)
apex: A Shared Component that wraps any REST/JSON web service or generic JSON feed as a reusable, discoverable data source usable by reports, charts, forms, LOVs and other APEX components exactly like a local table.
attributes: REST Data Sources page (Shared Components > Data Sources)
workflow: Define once in Shared Components, then pick it as the Data Source or Source Type for any report, chart, form, calendar or LOV.
relevance: This is the single most transferable concept in the whole data chapter: Paddock already fetches OpenF1, FOM API and ICS feeds ad hoc in code; a first-class external data source shared component is what Paddock Developer's data layer should formalize.

name: Creating a REST Data Source (wizard)
apex: Wizard that registers an external REST/JSON endpoint as a Shared Component, either sampling a live response (Discover) or an uploaded sample (Advanced) to auto-derive a Data Profile, or skipping discovery entirely (Manual).
attributes: REST Data Source Type: Simple HTTP/plug-in type
workflow: Shared Components > REST Data Sources > Create > enter the endpoint URL and auth, then choose Discover to auto-derive columns from a live or sample JSON/XML response.
relevance: Auto-deriving a typed schema, a Data Profile, from a live or sample API response is precisely the onboarding flow Paddock Developer should offer when an admin wires up a new external feed.

name: Remote Server (Base URL indirection for REST Data Sources)
apex: A separate reusable object storing just a base URL; a REST Data Source references a Remote Server plus a service-specific path suffix, so many data sources sharing one host can be repointed, e.g. test to production, by editing the Remote Server once.
workflow: Create a Remote Server with the host's base URL once, then build each REST Data Source by picking that Remote Server and adding only the path suffix.
relevance: Separating a shared base URL from each endpoint's path is exactly how Paddock Developer should let an admin swap an entire upstream host, e.g. a mirrored API, without editing every data source.

name: REST Data Source Pagination Types
apex: Five ways APEX can page through a REST API's results: none, page size plus offset, page size plus page number, page number only with a fixed size, or page size plus a continuation token.
workflow: Pick the pagination style that matches the target API's query parameters when creating or editing a REST Data Source's Settings.
relevance: Covers essentially every pagination style Paddock's own upstream feeds use (OpenF1 offset paging, FOM API, etc); a Paddock Developer data-source screen should offer the same named presets instead of custom code per feed.

name: REST Data Source on a REST Enabled SQL Query
apex: A REST Data Source type that executes an arbitrary SQL query against a remote database via a REST Enabled SQL reference, so results become an APEX data source with Discovery still deriving the Data Profile.
attributes: REST Data Source Type: REST Enabled SQL Query
workflow: Pick REST Enabled SQL Query as the type, choose an existing REST Enabled SQL Reference, write the SQL, then Discover to build the Data Profile.
relevance: Solves querying a remote relational database, e.g. MySQL, through Oracle's REST-enabled SQL bridge; Paddock has no such cross-database bridge requirement.
skip_for_web: REST Enabled SQL is an Oracle-specific remote-database bridge Paddock does not need

name: REST Data Source Operations
apex: Each REST Data Source has one or more Operations mapping a URL pattern and HTTP method to a logical Database Operation, so APEX components know which call is the fetch-list versus insert versus update, with a templated request body for write operations.
workflow: On the REST Data Source edit page, Add Operation, set its URL pattern and HTTP method, map it to a Database Operation, and template the request body for writes.
relevance: Mapping one external endpoint per logical action (list, insert, update) instead of one big client is the right shape for Paddock Developer to expose a write-capable external integration, not just read-only fetches.

name: REST Data Source Caching
apex: Per-operation server-side response caching for GET requests, with an Invalidate When setting, minutes or a recurring schedule string, controlling when cached results expire.
attributes: Invalidate When: minutes or DBMS_SCHEDULER Calendaring String
workflow: On a REST Data Source Operation, enable Caching and set an expiry window or recurring invalidation schedule to cut down repeated calls to the same external GET endpoint.
relevance: Server-side response caching with a scheduled invalidation is the model Paddock's own warm-live-data snapshot system already approximates; worth formalizing per data source in Paddock Developer.
skip_for_web: the DBMS_SCHEDULER calendaring string syntax itself is Oracle-specific

name: Deleting a REST Data Source
apex: A REST Data Source can only be deleted once no APEX component still references it.
workflow: REST Data Sources page > open the source > Delete; APEX refuses if any component still depends on it.
relevance: A hard reference-count guard against deleting an in-use data source is exactly the safety Paddock Developer needs before letting an admin delete a wired-up data source or component.

name: Copying or Subscribing to a REST Data Source (cross-app)
apex: Same cross-application copy and subscribe wizard already logged for other shared component types, applied to REST Data Sources.
relevance: Same copy and subscribe mechanism already logged multiple times; no new concept.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: Copying a REST Data Source (same app)
apex: Duplicates an existing REST Data Source within the same application under a new name via a dedicated Copy button.
workflow: REST Data Sources page > Copy > pick the source data source > name the copy > Copy.
relevance: Same same-app duplicate pattern already logged for Lists, Search Configurations and Report Layouts; no new concept.
skip_for_web: duplicate mechanism, different component type

name: Working with REST Data Sources for Oracle Cloud SaaS Applications (overview)
apex: Table-of-contents page for the Oracle Cloud SaaS and Fusion Applications REST Data Source subtopics.
relevance: Pure navigation page; content is covered in the linked subtopics.

name: Oracle Cloud SaaS REST Service Type Detection

attributes: REST Data Source Type: Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) REST Service
REST Data Source Type: Oracle Cloud Applications (BOSS) REST Service
workflow: Inspect the target endpoint's URL path to decide which built-in Oracle Cloud Applications REST Data Source type to select in the wizard.
relevance: Entirely about recognizing Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications, Visual Builder and ADF endpoint URL conventions; Paddock integrates with motorsport data APIs, not Oracle Fusion products.

name: Creating a REST Data Source for Oracle Cloud SaaS Apps
apex: Walks the same generic Create REST Data Source wizard, just with REST Data Source Type set to Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) REST Service and defaults accepted for Remote Server and Pagination.
relevance: Reuses the generic REST Data Source wizard already logged; the only difference is the Oracle-Fusion-specific Type selection.
skip_for_web: Oracle Fusion SaaS-specific wizard path

name: Auto-Generated CRUD Operations and Synthetic Resource Key
apex: When APEX builds a REST Data Source against a full CRUD endpoint, it wires up GET-list (filter/order/paginate), GET-by-key, POST, PATCH and DELETE operations automatically, and gives the Data Profile a synthetic APEX$RESOURCEKEY primary key so any resource's real identity scheme, single key, composite key, or alternate unique key, works uniformly.
attributes: Auto-created Operations: GET list/GET by key/POST/PATCH/DELETE
workflow: Point the wizard at a CRUD-capable endpoint; it derives all five operations and a normalized resource-key column without manual mapping.
relevance: A synthetic, normalized row-identity column so every external source looks the same to the framework regardless of its real key shape is a strong idea for Paddock Developer's own data-source abstraction.

name: Data Profile Column Visibility (trimming huge schemas)
apex: For endpoints exposing hundreds of attributes, APEX limits Data Profile columns actually fetched to a maximum of 150 Visible ones, prioritizing custom fields, while a developer can further delete, hide, or mark unused columns Never-rendered to cut payload size.
workflow: After discovery, review the auto-generated Data Profile and hide, delete, or condition-out columns a given region does not need, keeping requests small.
relevance: A visible-columns cap plus an explicit hide and delete step is exactly how Paddock Developer should let an admin tame a large external API schema down to only what a component actually renders.

name: Root Resource Name (nested child resources)
apex: A setting identifying which top-level resource a REST Data Source's rows logically belong to, needed when the data source targets a nested child collection, e.g. an employee's vacation requests, rather than a top-level object.
workflow: Leave blank for a top-level endpoint since APEX infers it; set explicitly when the data source targets a child resource nested under a parent object's URL.
relevance: Parent and child resource relationships, e.g. an event's sessions or a driver's results, are common in Paddock's data; explicitly naming the owning root resource is a useful idea for nested data sources.

name: Use Total Results? (pagination count)
apex: A REST Data Source setting controlling whether APEX asks the endpoint for a total row count so the UI can show 1-20 of 200; turned off for endpoints that cannot supply a count or do not support pagination at all.
workflow: Settings tab of a REST Data Source: set Use Total Results to Yes for a full count display, or Use Pagination to No if the endpoint returns everything at once.
relevance: An explicit toggle for whether pagination and total-count are even possible against a given feed is exactly the kind of per-source capability flag Paddock Developer needs for uneven external APIs.

name: External Filter and External Order Bys
apex: Region-level settings that push a SQL-like filter predicate or a comma-separated sort list down to a REST Data Source's endpoint for server-side execution, using the API's real case-sensitive attribute names and APEX substitution parameters for dynamic values.
workflow: On a region built from a REST Data Source, write a filter predicate or order-by list using the API's own field names; APEX substitutes page-item values and sends it to the remote service.
relevance: Pushing filter and sort down to the origin API instead of fetching everything and filtering client-side is exactly how Paddock Developer should let an admin query a large external feed, e.g. all-time results, efficiently.

name: Batch Lost Update Protection and Batch DML
apex: When a user saves many inserted, updated or deleted rows from a REST-backed region, APEX checks lost-update protection for all rows and then writes all changes in one all-or-nothing round trip to the endpoint, instead of one call per row; either behavior can be disabled per source if the endpoint cannot support it.
workflow: Leave Batch DML enabled for endpoints that accept multi-row payloads; disable it on the Settings tab to fall back to one call per changed row.
relevance: An all-or-nothing single-round-trip save for a batch of row edits, with a fallback to per-row calls, is a strong pattern for any Paddock Developer feature that lets an admin bulk-edit rows backed by an external API.

name: REST Validation Errors Surfaced Automatically
apex: Server-side validation failures or trigger errors from a REST Data Source's endpoint are automatically shown to the user as standard APEX error messages, with multiple errors joined by a br-tag delimiter.
workflow: No configuration needed: a rejected save from the remote endpoint surfaces its error text through the same error UI as any local validation failure.
relevance: Surfacing a remote API's validation errors through the exact same error banner as local validation, with no special-casing, is the right bar for Paddock Developer's own external-write error handling.

name: REST Data Source Filter Parameters (declarative QBE/cascading)
apex: A naming convention, attrName_operator$behavior, for GET-operation URL parameters that declaratively wires a REST Data Source's server-side filtering to page items, enabling cascading select lists and Query-By-Example pages with no procedural code.
workflow: Define a filter parameter like componentId_eq$norowsifnull on the data source, then bind it to a page item's LOV or a search region's field so filtering happens server-side with zero PL/SQL.
relevance: A declarative, name-encoded filter and operator and null-behavior contract is a clean way for Paddock Developer to expose cascading pickers, e.g. season then event, and search-by-example without hand-written filter code.

name: Working Against a Sandbox (Fusion Apps)
apex: Lets an APEX app point its Oracle Cloud SaaS REST Data Sources at a named Fusion Applications sandbox, a private unpublished customization branch, instead of the published production schema, by setting a sandbox name in Component Settings.
attributes: Component Settings > Oracle Cloud Applications (SaaS) REST Service > sandbox name
workflow: Set the sandbox name once at the app level; clear it to switch back to the published production endpoint.
relevance: Fusion Applications sandboxes are an Oracle SaaS customization-branching concept with no equivalent in Paddock's stack.
skip_for_web: Oracle Fusion Applications sandbox concept is product-specific

name: Rediscover Data Profile and Synchronize Columns
apex: A two-step workflow for picking up new fields added upstream: Rediscover refreshes a REST Data Source's Data Profile with any new attributes, then Synchronize Columns adds the new fields to a region while leaving already-commented-out columns untouched.
workflow: When the external schema gains fields, edit the Data Source and click Rediscover, then open the affected region and choose Synchronize Columns to add just the new fields.
relevance: A safe re-sync workflow that adds new upstream fields without disturbing a developer's existing column choices or comments is exactly what Paddock Developer needs when an external feed's schema grows.

name: Environment-Specific Base URL via Remote Server (DEV/PROD split)
apex: Best practice confirming the Remote Server's Base URL is the part of a REST endpoint that should change between environments, DEV vs PROD, while the Service URL Path stays identical; the Base URL value is sticky per target environment across app deployments and imports.
workflow: When building a REST Data Source, split its endpoint so everything that changes between DEV and PROD lives in the Remote Server's Base URL, and everything constant lives in the Service URL Path; redeploying the app then never touches the path.
relevance: Paddock already runs three environments, prod, testing and a paris preview, sharing infra; a base-URL-vs-path split that survives redeploys unchanged is the right model for any per-environment external endpoint in Paddock Developer.

name: Header-Type Parameters (per-source/operation HTTP header overrides)
apex: A REST Data Source or Operation Parameter of type Header lets a developer force a specific outgoing HTTP header value, overriding whatever APEX would send by default.
workflow: Add a module or operation parameter, set its Type to Header, name it after the real HTTP header, and give it the value to send on every request.
relevance: A generic per-source header override is a small but necessary escape hatch Paddock Developer's data-source screen needs for feeds requiring custom auth or versioning headers.
skip_for_web: the specific REST-Framework-Version and Metadata-Context sandbox headers are Oracle Fusion Applications specifics

name: Data Profile Column Annotations (Additional Info tags)
apex: Per-column tags on a Data Profile's Additional Info attribute that fine-tune how that column is sent in create and update requests: omit if null, exclude from updates, exclude entirely from writes, or flag as required.
workflow: Edit a Data Profile column's Additional Info field and add a comma-separated list of the relevant tags to change its write behavior.
relevance: This exact tag set, remote-generated key, create-only, read-only, has-a-default, required, is the right vocabulary for Paddock Developer's own field-level write-behavior settings on any external data source.

name: Discovering Endpoints That Require a Seed Filter
apex: A technique for endpoints that reject requests with no filter at all: temporarily hard-code one required-attribute query parameter with a throwaway value just to get a sample response for schema Discovery, then delete that hard-coded parameter and replace it with a real bound Filter Parameter.
attributes: Advanced > Parameters > Parameter Type: URL Query String (temporary seed value)
workflow: If Discover fails because the endpoint demands a filter, add a one-off query-string parameter with a dummy value to get past discovery, then remove it and add a proper Filter Parameter bound to a real page item.
relevance: A seed-then-replace trick for onboarding endpoints that refuse unfiltered requests is a useful edge case Paddock Developer's data-source wizard should anticipate for picky upstream APIs.
skip_for_web: the specific Fusion Apps error text and attribute names are product-specific

name: Discover References (auto-include related objects)
apex: A BOSS REST Data Source creation setting that, when enabled, pulls in the first level of an object's referenced (foreign-key) objects as additional read-only columns during discovery, alongside updateable accessor foreign-key columns for reassigning the reference by key.
workflow: Enable Discover References when creating the data source to get related-object fields for free; leave it off and add specific reference columns later by editing the Data Profile.
relevance: Auto-expanding one level of related-object fields, e.g. a result row pulling in its driver's name, as read-only, with a separate updateable key column, is a strong pattern for Paddock Developer's own relational data sources.

name: ETag Column for Optimistic Concurrency (APEX$ETAG)
apex: For versioned business objects, the Data Profile includes a synthetic APEX$ETAG column mapped to the endpoint's ETag or version indicator; APEX uses it to detect concurrent edits before allowing an update or delete.
workflow: When a business object tracks a version number, its auto-built Data Profile gets an ETag column automatically; APEX checks it on every update or delete to prevent overwriting someone else's concurrent change.
relevance: A first-class ETag or version column for optimistic concurrency is exactly the safeguard Paddock Developer needs before allowing edits to any externally-sourced or admin-shared row.

name: Additional Data Profile Column Tags (Sortable, AccessorFK, Subtype)
apex: Further Additional Info tags beyond the base set: Sortable marks a column as usable in sort requests, AccessorFK marks a column as the foreign key used to reassign a reference object, and Subtype excludes a field from responses and payloads entirely when null.
workflow: Add these tags to a Data Profile column's Additional Info when the wizard's automatic inference misses them; mainly HasDefault and Subtype need manual tagging.
relevance: Sortable and AccessorFK in particular round out the field-level metadata vocabulary Paddock Developer would want on any relational external data source.

name: Background Processing Monitor

name: Promoting a Locally Defined LOV to Shared
apex: A List of Values first defined inline on one item, a Locally Defined LOV, can later be converted into a named Shared Component once other pages need the same list.
attributes: Convert to shared list of values
workflow: Build a quick inline LOV on an item; once a second item needs the same options, find it under the Locally Defined tab and convert it to a shared List of Values.
relevance: Start-local-then-promote-to-shared is the natural authoring path for Paddock Developer: an admin defines options directly on one field, then promotes to a reusable list only once reuse is proven.

name: Component Settings as a Groupable Shared Component
apex: Component Settings, default configuration for native component types, is itself listed among the shared component types that can belong to a Component Group, alongside Lists, LOVs, REST Data Sources and others.
workflow: Include Component Settings entries when building a Component Group so a bundle's default settings travel with the rest of its components.
relevance: Confirms Paddock's own Component Settings feature (Phase 3, what a new region starts with) matches APEX's own concept and naming; it should be groupable and exportable alongside other shared components too.

name: Data Loading Volume Limits
apex: Guidance that the built-in Data Load wizard is meant for modest file sizes, not hundreds of thousands of rows; very large imports should use a dedicated bulk-loading tool instead.
workflow: Use the Data Loading page for typical admin uploads; for very large datasets, load via a script or direct database tool instead.
relevance: The same caution applies to Paddock Developer: a browser-based CSV importer is right for admin-sized uploads, e.g. a season's calendar, but should point to a script-based path for bulk historical backfills.

name: Data Profile
apex: The core schema-mapping object behind every JSON/XML-based data source, REST Data Source, Duality View, Data Load Definition: a Row Selector locates the collection of rows, and Data Profile Columns map each JSON or XML attribute to a typed, named column APEX components can bind to.
workflow: APEX derives a Data Profile automatically by sampling a live or uploaded response; a developer then edits, hides, deletes or annotates its columns to match what the app actually needs.
relevance: A single reusable schema-mapping abstraction, auto-discovered then hand-tuned, is the central design Paddock Developer's data layer should adopt for every external or semi-structured content source.

name: REST Source Plug-Ins (custom REST Data Source Types)
apex: Beyond the built-in Simple HTTP and Oracle Cloud types, a REST Data Source Type can be supplied by a REST Source Plug-In, letting a developer package a custom protocol or auth handshake as a reusable, selectable type.
workflow: Select a plug-in-provided type from the REST Data Source Type list instead of Simple HTTP when a specific external system needs custom handling.
relevance: A pluggable data-source-type mechanism is a good long-term extensibility model for Paddock Developer once more than a couple of bespoke upstream integrations exist.

name: Advanced Discovery from an Uploaded Response Sample
apex: An alternative to live Discovery: upload a saved sample JSON or XML response file and APEX derives the Data Profile from that file instead of calling the live endpoint.
workflow: When the live endpoint cannot be reached at design time (auth, network, or IP restrictions), upload a captured sample response instead and let APEX profile it offline.
relevance: Paddock's own upstream parsers already fail from some networks or IPs at design time; sample-based offline discovery is exactly the workaround Paddock Developer should offer for wiring up a data source when the live call cannot run locally.

name: REST Operation Parameters (dynamic URL/body values)
apex: Named parameters on a REST Data Source or a specific Operation that supply dynamic URL path segments, query-string values, headers, or request-body content; APEX components assign their values before each call.
attributes: Parameter Type: URL Query String/URL Pattern/Header/Body
workflow: Add Parameter on a Data Source or Operation, choose its type and name, then reference it from a page item or fixed value; APEX substitutes it into the request at runtime.
relevance: A typed, named parameter system for filling in URL segments, query strings, headers or body content from page items is the right general mechanism for Paddock Developer to expose configurable external calls.

name: Pass ECID (execution context tracing)
apex: An advanced REST Data Source setting that forwards APEX's internal Execution Context ID to the external web service as a header, enabling end-to-end request tracing across systems.
workflow: Enable Pass ECID on a REST Data Source when the target service can log or return the same trace ID, so a single request can be correlated across both systems' logs.
relevance: Forwarding a correlation or trace ID to every external call is a good observability habit Paddock Developer's data-source layer should support once multiple upstream integrations exist.

name: HTTP Transfer Timeout
apex: A per-REST-Data-Source setting bounding how long APEX waits while reading the HTTP response body, preventing a slow or hung upstream from blocking the application.
workflow: Set a transfer timeout on a REST Data Source to fail fast instead of hanging when the remote server or network is slow.
relevance: An explicit per-source timeout is a basic resilience control Paddock Developer's data-source settings should expose for every external integration.
